chunks: Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Suwayd al-Qallāʾ, from Abī Ayyūb, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said:

Indeed, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there are two knowledges: a knowledge that none knows except Him, and a knowledge that He taught to His angels and His Messengers. So whatever He taught to His angels and His Messengers (عليهم السلام), we know it.

key_terms.رُسُلَهُ: His Messengers; prophets sent by Allah who receive divinely taught knowledge
key_terms.عَلَّمَهُ: He taught it; knowledge bestowed by Allah upon chosen beings
key_terms.عِلْمَيْنِ: two knowledges; two categories or kinds of divine knowledge mentioned in the hadith
key_terms.فَنَحْنُ نَعْلَمُهُ: then we know it; the Imam's statement affirming their knowledge of what Allah taught His angels and Messengers
key_terms.لَا يَعْلَمُهُ إِلَّا هُوَ: none knows it except Him; knowledge exclusive to Allah alone
key_terms.لِلَّهِ: for Allah; indicating that all knowledge belongs to Him in origin and sovereignty
key_terms.مَلَائِكَتَهُ: His angels; among those to whom Allah discloses certain knowledge

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the knowledge of Allah and the knowledge granted to the Imams (عليهم السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, possesses two categories of knowledge: one exclusive to Him alone, and another that He discloses to His angels and Messengers. Imam Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) declares that the knowledge taught to the angels and Messengers is also known to them, indicating the elevated divinely granted knowledge of the Imams (عليهم السلام).

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Ali Bin Al Nu’man, from Suweyd Al Qalla’a, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘For Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic there are two (types of) Knowledges – a Knowledge which no one knows except Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and a Knowledge which He<sup>azwj</sup> Taught His<sup>azwj</sup> Angels, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasools<sup>as</sup>. So whatever He<sup>azwj</sup> Taught His<sup>azwj</sup> Angels and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasools<sup>as</sup>, so we<sup>asws</sup> know it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabber from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from Suwayd al-Qalla from abu Ayyub from abu Basir from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, has two kinds of knowledge. One kind of knowledge is that which no one knows except He. The other kind is that which He has taught to the His angels and His messengers. Whatever His angels and Messengers have learned we know it.”
